body:
CHANGES REQUESTED — TASK-1607 narrow launch-handshake amendment

Independent advisor: Codex task1607-launch-independent-advisor, native thread 01a11998-d392-7241-bdbb-1ad7928d1544, observed from this session environment. NEW Joe-assigned session; I authored neither this sketch nor any prior C7 review. Canonical role current --check returned advisor. AIDA_SESSION_ID is unset; no authenticated code-review grant or implementation lease is asserted. Date: 2026-10-07 America/Phoenix.

Reviewed canonical sketch comment 01a11997-3fca-7e32-88ba-2b329d2484c9, author task1607-launch-sketch-author: exactly one byte-equal match to TASK-1607-launch-handshake-sketch.md, including final newline; SHA256 22132f33f50fc481b01bfa2b068e46ec391625545aedf58cc2be6fbec80671e6. Source inspected read-only in /home/joe/ai/aida-worktrees/aida-task-1607, clean story-1485 at 56f7b55b32fba77a2b8bdbdd2573d59cce0ca29f. Main is separately 199e591b07aa76a59cd34f0a41946f918501f6ba. Canonical coordination uses only /home/joe/ai/aida/target/agent/aida.

Read AGENTS.md, two-seat/rework/recovery disciplines, aida-orchestrate sketch gate, full TASK-1607 and all 19 comments, signed faa07e4acb sketch and STORY-1485 signoff, ADR67–70/C1–C8 and refinements, C7_F3_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW.md, PRODUCTION_GATEWAYS_READY.md, PRODUCTION_GATEWAY_INVENTORY.md, production-audit/record-failure.log, the launch sketch and TASK1607_LAUNCH_SKETCH_READY.md. Also checked BUG-1808 common-substrate proposals and canonical independent decisions, including the newer v4 refusal 01a11999-4e97-7f12-b0f4-ba8dede0081f. That decision still blocks the callback-origin mechanism; v4 is not approved policy.

This is design review only. No build, tests, live launch, failure reproduction, source edit, commit/push, status/queue/grant/lease change, hold clearance or merge occurred. The diagnostic LIVE_CHILD_UNRECORDED=true RETRY_AUTHORIZED=true is inherited evidence, not a test I ran. C7 remains approved at the exact source SHA, checkpoint only. Production remains NOT READY.

Verified source and sound parts

runtime.rs::SeatPermit::record_child (105–141) receives a PID after spawn, substitutes an empty start on capture failure and saves afterward. store.rs::SeatGuard::save (123) calls fs_atomic::write_atomic (91), which writes/renames without fsync. run_tracked_agent (lib.rs:32512 onward) launches before register_spawned_agent. session.rs::spawn_vendor_headless_with_seat (1179), exec_vendor_headless (2769), and spawn_claude_headless_resume (3035) have differing issuance/spawn/wait paths. process_retry.rs retries ETXTBSY with sleeps; it supplies no execution barrier. ChildSpawn (mod.rs:139), SessionManifest (session_manifest.rs:77), and RunMarker (orchestrator.rs:88) do not supply the proposed reciprocal activation binding. internal_cmd.rs::handle_internal_command has no early bootstrap path. pane_host.rs::host_implementer_in_tmux (154) uses shell/rc rendezvous; agent_new_bg_dispatch explicitly leaves daemon PID ownership elsewhere. No current source mechanism closes the demonstrated gap.

The owned waiting bootstrap is the right direction: actual PID/start before vendor work, private sequenced channel with per-message credentials, parent-only one-shot release, durable binding before release, same-PID exec, and a final generation check serialized against takeover. Missing identity, binding, storage or channel proof must prevent release; Unknown must not become empty-start authority. All cleanup/wait/backoff stays outside the seat flock. Retain the distinction between never released and possibly executed: missing ACK/dead process cannot prove work never happened. None of these favorable findings constitutes amendment signoff while the two joins below are missing.

F1 — BLOCKING: define the common publisher/occupancy commit and refusal join

Affected proposed symbols: LaunchPublisher::{bind_waiting_child,release_bound_child}, PublicationGuard, SeatPermit::commit_waiting_child, verify_activation_for_exec; sketch steps 3–5 and BUG-1808 L2–L4/P4.

The sketch proposes durable shared receipt/seat binding, dropping ALL outer guards before RELEASE, then acquiring shared guards afresh in the child and rejecting expired/revoked issuer authority, changed assignment or seat generation before exec. BUG-1808's proposed L3 retains home through release, P4 is its sole authorization/COMMIT decision, and P4 explicitly forbids deferring delegation/refusal to vendor startup. Its binding earlier decision C retains unchanged-state acceptance for late authority refusal. The handshake proposal does not map its second authorization to this publication state machine or specify the disposition of already committed pickup setup when that authorization fails.

Concrete design counterexample: P4 and retained receipt become durable; parent drops home/seat; a supported revocation or seat transfer wins; RELEASE reaches the still-waiting child; final validation correctly refuses. Vendor sentinel is absent, but this invocation's published status/queue/worktree/grant/manifest setup remains. Rolling COMMIT back conflicts with publisher recovery; calling a fresh authority refusal an ordinary exec error silently narrows strict refusal acceptance. Likewise, merely retaining home per the old L3 deadlocks the child that now needs that same guard. These are design counterexamples, not reproduced runtime failures.

Required narrow revision: the BUG-1808 owner must supply one explicit shared state/lock/receipt transition table covering prepare, actual-PID bind, publication COMMIT, occupancy generation commitment, parent release, child final validation, cancellation and recovery. State exactly which predicates linearize at which boundary, who writes each durable observation, and what survives every pre/post-COMMIT refusal and crash. Resolve authority expiry/revocation and takeover races without weakening unchanged-state acceptance, reintroducing a seat reservation/Unknown wedge, waiting for a child under seat, or passing a process-local Rust guard across exec. Name exact superseded shared clauses; do not claim unsigned L3/P4 semantics are already accepted. If current acceptance cannot be satisfied, report that concrete conflict rather than reclassifying it away.

Binding order remains BUG-1808 common LaunchPublisher/publication/assignment/receipt substrate FIRST, independently implemented and verified; TASK-1607 adds occupancy integration as a consumer, BUG-1802 adds its later policy consumer. Neither consumer is a prerequisite to implementing the common transport. The precise production prerequisite includes the reciprocal process/grant/manifest/member/attempt join AND publication/refusal integration above, with the existing BUG-1808 callback-origin blocker resolved for paths requiring Git publication. A transport-only owned WaitingChild/channel/cancellation primitive can be separately designed under BUG-1808, exposing no authority, no persistent assignment schema and no vendor release without a publisher-issued committed binding token. That bounded component alone does not satisfy TASK-1607 or establish compatibility. This verdict does not authorize a competing launcher, approve BUG-1808 wholesale, or mutate canonical dependencies.

Required proposed witness: task1607_launch_publication_final_check_race, through actual queue-work/foreground and phase entrypoints with barriers after shared COMMIT/before RELEASE and before final exec lock. Race supported revocation, clock expiry, roster loss, generation transfer and member/attempt replacement. Assert the specified full lifecycle/history/receipt outcome, absent sentinel on refusal, intact peer changes, bounded recovery and no automatic replacement. Include valid controls. Exercise supported Git publication/recovery with production hooks; absence of deadlock in a transport-only fixture is insufficient.

F2 — BLOCKING: make executable pinning an executable mechanism

Affected proposed symbols: PreparedLaunch, spawn_waiting/bootstrap_main, verify_activation_for_exec, session::spawn_bound_vendor.

“Pinned AIDA executable”, “resolve exact executable”, and command/binding digest do not specify how the kernel executes the recorded image rather than re-resolving a mutable path. Source currently constructs Command from paths. Actual PID/start and SCM_CREDENTIALS authenticate a process/channel, not the later executable file. A path/symlink replacement between preparation and exec can preserve argv/digest text and the same PID/start while executing a different image. A declared credential-preserving target can also be replaced with one that clears parent-death protection. No malicious grant or seat-record edit is needed for this counterexample.

Required revision: specify the actual helper and vendor execution primitive and retained image identity. For example, a verified descriptor-backed executable with a defined immutable-content/identity check and execveat/fexecve semantics, or an equally concrete immutable artifact boundary. Define scripts/interpreters and wrapper chains separately: either pin the supported chain and its descriptor behavior or refuse that managed variant before setup. Check effective credential/capability behavior on the image actually executed; do not rely on a prior pathname stat. Define FD closure for control/error/description/executable and lock handles on successful exec and all errors, including script-interpreter close-on-exec limitations. Preserve intended containment; no silent unwrapped fallback. This is exact launch identity, not a request for a new general sandbox.

Required proposed witness: task1607_launch_exec_image_binding, with deterministic replacement of helper/vendor symlink or executable after prepare and after durable bind. Actual entrypoint must either execute the pinned recorded image or refuse without vendor sentinel; replacement must never run under the old digest. Add interpreter/wrapper and credential-changing negative cases plus matching compiled fake-vendor positive and FD inventory. A command-object assertion cannot prove this.

Preserved constraints and acceptance work

- ADR70 remains bounded local commitment, seat before queue. No mailbox/network/forge/Git hook work, READY/RELEASE wait, child completion, termination/reaping or ETXTBSY sleep under permanent seat flock. Every outer guard and callback acquisition must have one documented total order. The proposed local final exec check is viable only after F1 is resolved; no broad durable dispatch reservation is approved.
- Storage fault coverage must distinguish pre-rename failure from visible-but-not-durably-confirmed post-rename/file/directory-sync failure. No release token on any failure. Retained receipts and later seat-record replacements must preserve durable live-child evidence; cleanup cannot overwrite peer state or erase possibly executed attempts.
- Parent-death protection must cover the creating thread, pre-prctl race, credential changes and same-PID exec. Retain identity-bound cancellation on every parent drop/error path and a defined orphan reaping owner after parent death; a dead parent cannot itself reap. No peer signaling or guessed bare-PID cleanup. See Linux PR_SET_PDEATHSIG documentation: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/PR_SET_PDEATHSIG.2const.html . Channel credentials and FD semantics were checked against https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/unix.7.html and https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/execve.2.html . These mechanisms do not prove retroactive nonexecution after exec; retained evidence and explicit retry/resume remain mandatory.
- Foreground requires actual bootstrap-to-vendor identity; headless/fresh/reviewer/resume requires one issuance owner and corroborated resume lineage; former CLI exec requires an actual supervising parent or pre-bound activation. Phase consumers require token/member/phase/attempt plus child grant join, not shared current or inherited driver authority. Pane/PTY requires its own authenticated actual-parent/host-PID adapter. Native daemon remains pre-setup unsupported refusal. Unsupported OS/namespace/containment mappings also refuse before setup; wrapper PID is never vendor evidence. Temporary refusal is not full positive gateway acceptance.
- Proposed first-action-sentinel matrix otherwise covers before/after record, RELEASE, parent death, storage faults, stale/duplicate/wrong-child release, identity Unknown, bounded same-attempt retry, assigned child scope and C8. Preserve each matching actual-entrypoint positive, deterministic barriers, guard-removal/restoration nonvacuity, snapshot of full lifecycle and peer state, and no live peers as targets. Add F1/F2 witnesses above and orphan cleanup/reaping assertions. None has been run by this review.
- Preserve all eight C7 criteria and F1/F2/F3 fixes, disabled kill, no grant/TTY-floor widening, TASK-1337 role/delegation/branch-before-setup and manual continuation, TASK-1603 token-specific registration-before-status/launch, every production inventory row, timer/redrive disposition and UUID-idempotent existing-history projection. The 1321 candidate scan is not semantic coverage proof. No new ledger substitutes for existing history obligations.

Disposition: CHANGES REQUESTED for F1 and F2. Return a narrow revised common commit/refusal join and exact executable-binding mechanism to a different advisor. No source implementation of this amendment is authorized by this verdict. Existing C7 checkpoint approval is not revoked; full TASK-1607 remains incomplete and production NOT READY. No requested requeue is performed because Joe explicitly prohibited queue changes. Joe's sandbox bypass applied only to the worker; it grants no authority bypass here. Final authority-sensitive merge and any operator authorization remain Joe's.

Canonical comment/readback and advisor notification receipts are saved separately in TASK1607_LAUNCH_INDEPENDENT_SIGNOFF_RECEIPT.json so this exact verdict body remains byte-identical to its canonical comment.
subject: TASK-1607 launch amendment: CHANGES REQUESTED; exact canonical readback verified
